idea_recap: Opening a second physical location instead of continuing to focus delivery and dine-in from a single kitchen.

supporting_signals.signal: Both Bar-B-Q Tonight and Butt Karahi operate multiple locations, and multi-branch presence is part of how they signal scale and trust.
supporting_signals.reasoning: This suggests that in this category, multiple locations is a recognized path to legitimacy and reach once a concept is proven.

supporting_signals.signal: FirePit's current positioning (shareable platters, group/delivery occasions) doesn't depend on a specific single location's foot traffic in the way a dine-in-first concept would.
supporting_signals.reasoning: A delivery-and-group-order-oriented model may transfer to a second kitchen more easily than a dine-in-destination model would.

risk_signals.signal: FirePit is still early-stage, and both cited competitors are established, multi-branch operations -- their expansion likely came after years of single-location proof, not before it.
risk_signals.reasoning: Expanding before the first location has a fully proven, consistent operation risks diluting quality and brand consistency across two sites simultaneously.

risk_signals.signal: No visible evidence in the competitor data about what specifically justified their expansion timing (demand overflow, delivery radius limits, etc.).
risk_signals.reasoning: Without knowing why they expanded when they did, it's hard to tell if FirePit is at an analogous point yet.

competitor_parallels.observation: Positions heavily on brand legacy and a wide branch network -- suggests multi-location is core to how they compete, but this took years of being an established name first.
Also multi-location with a value/portion-size positioning -- similar pattern, no visible signal on how early they expanded relative to launch.

suggested_next_step: Before opening a second kitchen, test whether the real constraint is delivery radius/capacity at the current location (which a second kitchen would fix) or something else (brand awareness, menu, pricing) -- a second location only solves the first problem.
caveat: This is informed reasoning based on a business profile and two competitors' visible homepage content, not market research or a guarantee this will work -- worth testing the underlying assumption before committing further.
